title: Needs a serious update
body: I climbed 700 stairs, and this app told me I did 9 flights!!! Sorry, 700 stairs is between 47-58 flights!  I use the stairs in my building going down 30 and up 30.  It gives me me 2 flights of if I do both up/down flights, but won’t acknowledge either 1 of 30 stairs up or down.  Calories is off.  It needs to read heart rate more accurately because when carrying something and/or in hot weather calories expended go UP.  Other exercises besides running, hiking or brisk walking are not acknowledged correctly.  I use my workout app in tandem with this and can work out for over an hour and this app gives me credit for 35-40 minutes.  Please, update!!!
author: Molly Swift Healy

title: Why Is the iPad Version So Limited?
body:
★☆☆☆☆

The iPad version of the Fitness app is a huge disappointment compared to the iPhone version. Instead of being a proper companion for Apple Watch, it mostly pushes Fitness+ content while important activity features are missing or much harder to access. It feels incomplete and unnecessarily limited. Apple should bring the iPad app up to the same standard as the iPhone version.

title: More configuration options and longer yoga classes
body:
The app is great and the yoga classes are nice, however., there are some missing options that would elevate  the app to a useful fitness app 
1. regulate music volume or choose playlist 
Especially during yoga but also other exercises the music volume is quite loud and even with choosing the audio focus on the trainer  the music can be quite loud and difficult to understand the coach.
2. schedule classes - bring able to schedule classes into you iCal would be fabulous to keep on track and consistent (other apps offer that and it makes a big difference)
3. 60 minute yoga 
One 60 minute yoga class per month or quarter would be great for that longer workout, deeper focus and more calm. 

Thank you

title: Users should have more control over Background music volume
body: Yoga is a meditative form of exercise. The background music should be in sync with the form of exercise. Only instructor Jessica seems to understand this as her playlist is not disruptive and does not interrupt with the flow state. As a user either I need to have control over the background music   Volume or instructors need to choose their playlist wisely one which is in sync with the flow and not interfere with it.

title: Shocking that somebody’s job is to make this
body: Somehow this app ended up on my iPhone a few months ago and I’ve engaged with it a few times out of curiosity. It spams me a lot during the day which I wouldn’t mind if the info was correct. I have a garmin watch which I connected to the app and it clearly shows it is synced but they don’t seem to know each other. I ran 20 miles today and it is telling me I haven’t met my move goal for the ring thing🙄. Shocking that somebody’s job is to make a fitness app and then when I leave my phone in the car it has no idea what I am at. Everybody that is into fitness nowadays has a watch tracker. Joke of an app and an embarrassment to whoever thought it was ready for market.

title: Great for busy people
body:
I’ve used the app for about 18 months and love it. By far the best thing about Apple Fitness+ are the trainers. I have yet to come across a dud. They must all take happy pills, they are so positive and encouraging.
The variety of trainers and workouts make it easy to use and fit into a busy life. My only complaints are that I think you should be able to use it on a MacBook as a phone screen is way too small.  Also I’d love to see classes for flexibility as I find the mindful cool-downs not long enough. 
Great fitness app which is getting better with new trainers and workouts being added all the time. It works for me!

title: Do not purchase fitness+ if you don’t have a big ipad
body:
The fact you can’t airplay to a 2000€ MacBook makes this subscription pretty much worthless.
The iPhone screen is too small to see and learn the moves, while travelling you can’t really carry your Apple TV with you, and having an iPad, iPhone and MacBook is really unnecessary. Unless you already have an iPad, look for another fitness app that works with airplay or that’s available to be streamed on your MacBook. 
+1 star for the workouts though. They’re good.
